title: Timing a possible encounter
target: Separate orbital period from an encounter time.
criteria: Use a clearly stated period and time reference.
Check positions of both bodies at the same time.
Explain why geometry and uncertainty matter.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A toy orbit repeats every 6 years, with an object at marker Q in year 3. When are its next two returns?
cpa.guide: Add the period to the stated reference year each time.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Two orbit predictions quote the same period but use different starting epochs. What else must be matched to compare positions?
options: Orbital phase or position at a common time reference.
cpa.guide: A period tells repetition duration, not where a body is at a chosen time.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Two orbital paths cross geometrically. What is required for a collision at the crossing?
options: Both bodies must reach the same place at the same time.
Either body reaches the crossing at any date.
cpa.guide: A path crossing alone does not establish simultaneous occupancy.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A toy object reaches crossing C in year 10. Earth reaches C in years 9.5 and 10.5. Does this establish a collision at year 10?
options: No; orbiting bodies can never collide.
Yes; half a year is the same instant.
Yes; a shared crossing guarantees collision.
No; the listed arrivals are not simultaneous.
cpa.guide: Compare positions at matching times, not just shared geometry.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: Why should an encounter prediction include uncertainty?
options: Small initial-position or velocity uncertainties can affect later predicted positions.
cpa.guide: Predictions depend on imperfect measurements and models.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Which evidence is most useful beyond period for assessing a close approach?
options: Orbit orientation, size/shape, phase, and uncertainty at the same epoch.
cpa.guide: Geometry and synchronized position estimates are needed to evaluate separation.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
